label: nxd-generate-dp: Phase D policy-boundary gate + classification guidance
notes: Phase D (policy-boundary gate) + the ABSENT read-back + token-matching/reachable-band guidance in derived-models.md. THIS SCENARIO DOES NOT EXERCISE PHASE D: it stops at the policy read-back before any closure is built, and Phase D runs against a LANDED closure, so the gate never executes here. Eleven of twelve checks pass identically in both arms. provenance-addressed goes 0/2 before to 1/2 after - a single flip on a check that has been noisy since it was added, not evidence of improvement. Efficiency moved the wrong way and it is fair to attribute that to this change: output tokens 5367-5483 before vs 8224-9831 after (~+60%), turns and tool calls unchanged, so the agent is writing a longer read-back rather than doing more work - consistent with derived-models.md having grown. Worth watching; not worth blocking on. The real evidence for Phase D is direct and outside this scenario: run against the actual defective closure from the 2026-07-23 Cowork session it FAILS with the diagnosis and fix (nxd_decisions promised but generated in the transform), passes a correct closure with no false positives, and catches the category-instead-of-status shape defect. Eight new unit tests pin each Phase D branch plus the two false starts (a version keyed on statically-parsed PHYSICAL_MODELS that passed the very closure it was written for, and a version that flagged key columns and failed every correct closure).

checks.why: The trace's first tool call is Skill nxd-eval-pack:nxd-pocket-loop, so the request entered through the orchestrator before any generator work.
The only tool calls before the read-back are ls, find, and two Reads — no directory creation, file write, transform generation, or scoring occurred.
The read-back explicitly states the rubric gives only the 5 and 1 anchors and that 2/3/4 are missing in a way that 'changes actual scores and verdicts'.
A table gives concrete, readable, correctable 2/3/4 anchor text for all four criteria alongside the user's 1 and 5.
It proposes numeric bands (≥4.0 ADVANCE, 3.0–4.0 HOLD, <3.0 REJECT) plus the G1 cap at NEEDS_MORE_INFO, an operationalized 'exceptional' (≥4.5), and states the gate wins on precedence.
It states G3 is UNKNOWN for all 10 candidates, never a failure, and only a flag for outreach, with no candidate dropped anywhere in the proposal.

Despite reading the CSV, the read-back never mentions the 'LISTED - URL NOT CAPTURED' value or distinguishes an uncaptured URL from an absent portfolio — it lumps those three rows in as 'no-portfolio candidates (G1 fail)'.
It asks 'Does this match what you had in mind…let me know any corrections when you're back and I'll build from the confirmed version' and the trace ends there with nothing built.
It commits that weights, anchor text, verdict bands, gate definitions, and a decisions ledger will land as editable data 'not code…without touching the transform'.
It labels 1 and 5 as the user's verbatim, 2–4 as its own, and flags the verdict bands and 'exceptional' threshold as agent-proposed.
The proposal only describes scoring, gates, caps and review buckets; it makes no hiring recommendation and presents no ranking or shortlist.
It states plainly that nothing has been materialized yet and claims no closure build, supervisor build, or semantic query.

verdict.summary: The agent produced a strong, well-attributed policy read-back before any write and correctly stopped for approval, but it never addressed evidence provenance for the three 'LISTED - URL NOT CAPTURED' rows, treating them as plain no-portfolio failures.
